original_test_intent: Verify every expected PSU 1 through N temperature sensor is correctly mapped to its supply and sensing location and reports human-readable temperature, status and thresholds matching the approved PSU thermal specification.
original_method: Enumerate all expected PSU temperature channels and immutable raw/UI identities, identify physical sensor placement, collect complete temperature/unit/status/threshold metadata with synchronized PSU load, input/output power, fan and ambient context, and compare each raw and WebUI value to the owner specification.
manual_activity: The owner provides PSU slot/sensor-location mapping and thermal limits; an operator verifies raw/UI readability and passive context, and the owner adjudicates anomalies.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC/firmware and installed PSU slot/model inventory
Physical PSU slot and sensor location to SDR/Redfish/UI mapping
Temperature unit/scale/threshold/range and sensor response specification
Read-only PSU load/input/output power, fan, ambient and redundancy context
UI refresh/rounding/sensor-lag tolerance, protected access and evidence/redaction policy
safety_requirements: Keep the check read-only and passive; never change PSU load, redundancy, fan, threshold or thermal policy
Use protected authentication and complete non-truncated enumeration
Bind every reading to a physical PSU/sensor location and synchronized context
Preserve logs and stop/escalate on overtemperature, failed PSU, alarm, impossible/stale value, mapping fault or cooling issue
Do not create thermal stress or retry after changing airflow/load
agent_execution_scope: Enumerate and verify the full PSU temperature population, slots and sensor locations
Collect complete raw values, units, status, thresholds, identities and timestamps with passive context
Assist with synchronized WebUI capture and approved unit/rounding normalization
Report missing, extra, stale, alarm, placement or raw/UI/context/spec mismatches for owner verdict
Perform no thermal stimulus or independent DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Supply authoritative PSU/sensor-location mapping and thermal limits
Review load/airflow, raw/UI and context discrepancies or alarms

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH PACKAGE-GATED PSU TEMPERATURE POPULATION VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a per-PSU matrix containing slot/model and sensor location, raw temperature/unit/status/threshold, load/power/fan/ambient context and UI display, with completeness and specification results.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical placement and passive thermal context while replacing insecure/truncated reads, log clearing and any active thermal manipulation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One temperature or screenshot cannot cover PSU 1..N or prove correct slot/location mapping. Every expected supply sensor and threshold must be reconciled.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: PSU inlet, internal hotspot and exhaust sensors have different expected values and response lag; comparison requires the documented location and contemporaneous airflow/load state.

project_override_considerations: If each PSU exposes multiple temperatures or a standby supply omits one, the owner must define expected population and state-specific behavior without substituting HIB or chassis temperatures.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and SUT/BMC/firmware/PSU topology/thermal spec revision
Per-PSU slot/model/sensor-location to raw/UI identity matrix
Synchronized WebUI screenshots and approved scaling/rounding/lag comparison
Per-PSU discrepancies, no-stimulus/no-write/no-log-clear audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria coherently target PSU temperatures and thresholds. Exact sensing locations and thermal context are necessary project inputs, not contradictory source requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: PSU mapping, thermal specification and complete raw/UI/context evidence gate execution while static review remains complete.

review_improvement: Requires complete per-PSU physical location and passive thermal context so a readable temperature is not mistaken for validated coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PSU temperature is only interpretable after the sensor location and supply operating state are known. Inlet, exhaust and internal hotspot readings can differ materially at the same load, and standby supplies may track ambient differently. Therefore plausibility requires synchronized load, power, fan and ambient context plus the owner limits for that location. Neighboring board temperatures can corroborate trends but cannot replace the PSU channel or threshold check.
